quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Same start and finish. Listen to the lips inside the vowel: rounded or spread?
quests.explanation: "Sock" has round lips and a deep vowel, with the sound pulled back into the mouth. "Sack" is bright and wide, with the lips slightly spread.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /æ/ is a front vowel with lips slightly spread; /ɒ/ is a back vowel with the lips rounded a little. The tongue moves from front to back and the lip shape changes with it.
quests.mouthPosition: For /æ/ keep the tongue pushed forward and the lips slightly spread. For /ɒ/ pull the tongue back and round the lips a little.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The consonants match. Does the vowel sound bright and open, or deep and round?
quests.explanation: What you caught was "pat": the jaw drops and the lips spread, giving a clear, bright vowel. In "pot" the mouth rounds and the vowel sounds darker.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Contrast the vowel colour: /æ/ sounds bright and sideways, /ɒ/ sounds deep and rounded.
quests.mouthPosition: Move your lips from a slight smile (/æ/) to a small round shape (/ɒ/) while the jaw stays open.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Ends in the same hollow stop. Focus on the vowel just before it.
quests.explanation: "Rock" keeps the lips rounded and the vowel deep. "Rack" spreads the mouth and brightens the sound.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Front and unrounded for /æ/; back and lightly rounded for /ɒ/. Both are open, so listen for brightness rather than height.
quests.mouthPosition: Notice where the sound seems to resonate: at the front of the mouth for /æ/, deeper in the mouth for /ɒ/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Say both in your head: which one needs a wide jaw?
quests.explanation: "Cup" is short and relaxed, and the jaw hardly opens. "Cap" needs a wide-open jaw and comes out fuller.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /æ/ is a front, open vowel made with the jaw low and lips slightly spread; /ʌ/ is a central, relaxed vowel that needs far less mouth opening.
quests.mouthPosition: For /æ/ drop the jaw and pull the corners of the mouth a little sideways. For /ʌ/ keep the mouth relaxed and only slightly open, with the tongue resting in the middle.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Same ending, different vowel weight. Listen for dull or bright.
quests.explanation: "Much" has a flat, dull vowel from the centre of the mouth. "Match" is brighter and wider, with the jaw dropped.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The tongue is forward and low for /æ/, but sits in the centre of the mouth for /ʌ/. To the ear, /æ/ sounds brighter and /ʌ/ sounds duller and flatter.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel the front of your tongue rise toward your teeth for /æ/; for /ʌ/ the tongue stays lazy and flat.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen just before the nasal ending: wide and bright, or dull and short?
quests.explanation: That was "hung", a short central vowel with the jaw relaxed. "Hang" would open the mouth wider and sound brighter.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Think 'wide and bright' for /æ/ against 'short and dull' for /ʌ/.
quests.mouthPosition: A big, wide mouth makes /æ/; a small, lazy mouth makes /ʌ/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Lips again: rounded or neutral? The rest of the word is identical.
quests.explanation: "Bus" leaves the lips neutral and the vowel flat. "Boss" adds gentle lip rounding and a deeper sound.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɒ/ is a back vowel with slight lip rounding; /ʌ/ is a central vowel with neutral lips. /ɒ/ sounds rounder and deeper, /ʌ/ sounds flatter and more central.
quests.mouthPosition: For /ɒ/ round the lips lightly and pull the tongue back. For /ʌ/ keep the lips neutral and let the tongue lie in the centre.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen for a rounded, back vowel or a neutral, central one.
quests.explanation: The word was "shot", with slightly rounded lips and the vowel pulled back. "Shut" is flatter and made in the middle of the mouth.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both are short, so rely on lip shape: rounded for /ɒ/, unrounded for /ʌ/.
quests.mouthPosition: Notice your lips: a small circle for /ɒ/, a neutral shape for /ʌ/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both end with the same hollow /k/. What is different in the vowel?
quests.explanation: "Luck" uses neutral lips and a short, central vowel. "Lock" rounds the lips and pulls the vowel back.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Tongue back and lips rounded make /ɒ/; tongue central and lips unrounded make /ʌ/.
quests.mouthPosition: Say /ʌ/ with a relaxed jaw and no lip tension; add gentle rounding to move toward /ɒ/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both are short. Is the jaw a little open or nearly closed?
quests.explanation: "Bet" opens the jaw slightly and sounds fuller. "Bit" keeps the teeth almost together and sounds thinner.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɪ/ is short and high-ish with the jaw nearly closed; /e/ is also short but the jaw opens further and the tongue lowers toward the middle.
quests.mouthPosition: For /ɪ/ keep the jaw almost shut with relaxed lips. For /e/ lower the jaw slightly so a fingertip could fit between the teeth.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen to the vowel before the /l/ - tight or a little more open?
quests.explanation: It was "well": the jaw drops just a bit further than for "will", which sounds tighter and softer.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The vowels are close, so listen for jaw opening: /ɪ/ feels tight and closed, /e/ feels a little more open.
quests.mouthPosition: Say /ɪ/ with hardly any jaw movement, then drop the jaw a little for /e/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Short vowels, almost the same. Feel the jaw height as you imagine each.
quests.explanation: "Led" needs a half-open jaw and a clear vowel. "Lid" is thin, quick and nearly closed.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /e/ sounds fuller and clearer, /ɪ/ sounds thinner and softer.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the tongue tip near the lower front teeth in both; only the height of the tongue body changes.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The vowel and ending are the same. What happens at the very start?
quests.explanation: "Mine" starts with the lips closed in a hum. "Nine" starts with the tongue tip touching the ridge, and the lips stay open.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /m/ is a nasal made with both lips closed; /n/ is a nasal made with the tongue tip touching the ridge. Both are voiced; the place of closure differs.
quests.mouthPosition: For /m/ close the lips and hum. For /n/ open the lips and touch the tongue tip to the ridge behind the teeth.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Focus only on the first sound. Lips or tongue?
quests.explanation: You heard "nail": the tongue tip touched the ridge behind the teeth. In "mail" the lips would have closed instead.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Lip closure for /m/, tongue closure for /n/.
quests.mouthPosition: Watch your lips: they close for /m/ and stay open for /n/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen to the hum at the start: does it come from the lips or the tongue tip?
quests.explanation: "Moon" begins with a rounded, lip-closed hum. "Noon" begins with the tongue-tip hum, which is a little brighter.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /m/ sounds rounder and darker; /n/ sounds brighter.
quests.mouthPosition: Hum the sound first, then open into the vowel.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The first sound is either a burst or a hum. Which do you catch?
quests.explanation: "Make" starts with a nasal hum through the nose. "Bake" starts with a burst of air as the lips pop apart.
quests.vowelTensionRule: A nasal consonant lets voiced air escape through the nose, while its oral partner blocks the nose and releases air from the mouth. Listen for a hum versus a burst.
quests.mouthPosition: For the nasal keep the nose open and hum; for the stop close off the nose and release air from the mouth. The lips or tongue tip make the same closure for both.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen for a hum at the start versus a pop.
quests.explanation: That was "beat": the lips popped open with a small burst. "Meat" would begin with a continuous hum instead.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Nasals have a continuous, humming quality; stops have a silent closure and a sudden release.
quests.mouthPosition: Pinch your nose: the nasal sound stops, but the oral stop does not.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Try pinching your nose in your head: would the first sound survive?
quests.explanation: "Mend" starts with a nasal hum that flows straight into the vowel. "Bend" starts with a lip pop.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The soft palate is lowered for nasals and raised for stops.
quests.mouthPosition: Hum the sound before the vowel.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Two-syllable words with the stress on the first part. The difference is the opening sound.
quests.explanation: The word was "coffee": the back of the tongue lifted for the /k/ at the start. "Toffee" opens with the tongue tip instead.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The alveolar stop is made with the tongue tip at the ridge behind the upper teeth; the velar stop is made with the back of the tongue at the soft palate. The velar release sounds deeper and more hollow.
quests.mouthPosition: For the alveolar stop touch the tongue tip to the ridge. For the velar stop lift the back of the tongue against the soft palate.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The beat falls on the first syllable. Listen to the vowel in that stressed part.
quests.explanation: "Butter" has the short, flat vowel in its strong syllable. "Batter" widens the jaw for a brighter, fuller vowel.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /æ/ is a front, open vowel made with the jaw low and lips slightly spread; /ʌ/ is a central, relaxed vowel that needs far less mouth opening.
quests.mouthPosition: For /æ/ drop the jaw and pull the corners of the mouth a little sideways. For /ʌ/ keep the mouth relaxed and only slightly open, with the tongue resting in the middle.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The ending is weak. Listen to the strong first syllable only.
quests.explanation: It was "summer", where the strong syllable is dull and relaxed. "Simmer" is thinner and brighter.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɪ/ is a front vowel with the tongue high and forward; /ʌ/ is a central vowel with the tongue low and relaxed. /ɪ/ sounds thinner and brighter, /ʌ/ sounds thicker and duller.
quests.mouthPosition: For /ɪ/ keep the jaw nearly closed and the tongue up toward the front. For /ʌ/ open a little more and let the tongue sink flat in the middle.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: One vowel moves and one stays put. Which is it?
quests.explanation: "Wait" slides upward and ends with the jaw closing. "Wet" stops right where it started, short and crisp.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /e/ is a short, steady vowel; /eɪ/ is longer and glides upward toward /ɪ/ so the sound changes as it goes. Listen for a vowel that stays still versus one that moves.
quests.mouthPosition: For /e/ hold the mouth half open and stop. For /eɪ/ start in the same place, then let the jaw close and the tongue rise as you finish.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen for a vowel that glides, and note how long it lasts.
quests.explanation: What you caught was "let": short, steady, with no glide. "Late" would stretch out and slide toward /ɪ/.
quests.vowelTensionRule: A pure vowel (/e/) keeps one position; a diphthong (/eɪ/) slides and ends with a small 'ee' closing.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel the jaw close during /eɪ/; during /e/ it stays put.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Focus on the vowel just before the nasal. Does it slide?
quests.explanation: "Pain" glides, closing the jaw as it goes. "Pen" is a compact, single-position vowel.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The ending is the giveaway: /eɪ/ finishes with the tongue and jaw rising, /e/ just stops.
quests.mouthPosition: Start with /e/, keep going, and slide the tongue up toward the roof of the mouth - that is /eɪ/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Do the lips move during the vowel, or stay still?
quests.explanation: "Note" begins relaxed and the lips close toward the end. "Not" is short and steady, with the lips only slightly rounded.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɒ/ is a short, steady back vowel; /əʊ/ starts in the centre and glides toward a rounded /ʊ/, so it is longer and moving. One holds still, the other travels.
quests.mouthPosition: For /ɒ/ open the jaw, round slightly and stop. For /əʊ/ start with relaxed lips and gradually round them into a small circle as you say it.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen for a two-part vowel against a short single one.
quests.explanation: You heard "goat": the sound started open and slid into a rounded finish. "Got" would be quick and steady.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Listen for a glide: /əʊ/ ends with the lips closing into an 'oo', while /ɒ/ finishes at once.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel the lips tighten during /əʊ/; during /ɒ/ they stay in one position.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The vowel length gives it away as much as the glide.
quests.explanation: "Rob" is short with no movement. "Robe" is longer, and the lips slowly round.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /əʊ/ is a diphthong and /ɒ/ is a short vowel; the diphthong sounds like it has two parts.
quests.mouthPosition: Say 'oh' slowly: the lips close toward the end. That movement is missing in /ɒ/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Bright and thin, or dull and thick? Listen to the vowel colour.
quests.explanation: "Dug" sounds duller and lower, with the tongue lying flat in the centre. "Dig" is brighter and tighter.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Tongue position separates them: forward and high for /ɪ/, central and low for /ʌ/. The result is a bright versus a dull vowel colour.
quests.mouthPosition: Relax the whole mouth for /ʌ/; for /ɪ/ lift the front of the tongue slightly toward the hard palate.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: This time the vowel matches. What does the tongue do at the very end?
quests.explanation: The word was "lot": the tongue tip closed against the ridge. "Lock" would end with the back of the tongue lifting.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Final /k/ is closed at the back of the tongue and /t/ at the tip. The closure position changes the very end of the vowel: deeper and duller into /k/, brighter into /t/.
quests.mouthPosition: For /k/ finish by lifting the back of the tongue to the soft palate. For /t/ finish with the tip against the ridge behind the teeth.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Focus on the first sound only. Is there a burst, or just breath?
quests.explanation: "Hold" begins with a soft breath of air. "Cold" begins with a closure at the back of the tongue and a tiny puff.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /k/ closes the back of the tongue against the soft palate and releases a burst; /h/ is only breath from the throat with nothing closing the mouth.
quests.mouthPosition: For /k/ lift the back of the tongue and release with a puff. For /h/ keep the tongue relaxed and just breathe out.
